correctness.rationale: Starting from the exact scope of Tian Theorem 4.1, rank-one decompositions lead to u v z^2 <= lambda mu as a necessary and sufficient feasibility condition. The commutator norm is u v z sqrt(1-z^2). The fixed-ratio maximization and bound via discriminant >= (u+v)z, AM-GM, and unique f(z) maximum at z=1/2 were reconstructed. The exact positive definite witness has a rank-one positive completion and commutator norm sqrt3/9. Boundary cases with scalar or commuting inputs are excluded by hypotheses; endpoints of the allowed z interval were checked. Included computations are supplementary only.

value.rationale: It answers the natural quantitative gap left by the first complete two-dimensional joint bilinear-resolvent moment criterion: how far the marginal operators may fail to commute. The full two-parameter spectral-gap envelope identifies a genuine constraint-saturated to overlap-saturated transition, while a sharp global 1/(3 sqrt3) rigidity constant gives a simple compatibility obstruction. This is an exact natural operator invariant, not an arbitrary numerical slice or recomputation of a known matrix table; it does not claim a general higher-dimensional result.
